The **XML** standard library parses a document and queries it with element
paths. `Parse XML` returns the root; `Get Elements` selects many by path;
`Get Element` selects exactly one — so when several match, index it, e.g.
`product[1]`. Work against the bundled `sample_data/catalog.xml`.

## Task 1 — Parse the catalog and query its elements

**Goal:** create `checks/xml.robot` that parses the catalog, counts its
`product` elements, and reads the name of the first one.

Here is the same parse-count-read flow over a small inline document. Adapt it to
the catalog file.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    XML

*** Test Cases ***
Parse A Small Document
    ${root}=    Parse XML    <shop><item>Pen</item><item>Cup</item></shop>
    ${items}=    Get Elements    ${root}    item
    Length Should Be    ${items}    2
    ${first}=    Get Element    ${root}    item[1]
    Should Be Equal    ${first.text}    Pen
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite imports `XML` and defines `Catalog Has Four Products`.

<!-- hint -->
`Parse XML` also takes a path: `${root}=    Parse XML    sample_data/catalog.xml`.
Then `Get Elements    ${root}    product` and `Length Should Be    ${products}    4`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Read the first product's name with a nested path:
`Get Element    ${root}    product[1]/name`, then assert
`Should Be Equal    ${first.text}    Trail Backpack`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    XML

*** Test Cases ***
Catalog Has Four Products
    ${root}=    Parse XML    sample_data/catalog.xml
    ${products}=    Get Elements    ${root}    product
    Length Should Be    ${products}    4
    ${first}=    Get Element    ${root}    product[1]/name
    Should Be Equal    ${first.text}    Trail Backpack
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** four products are found and the first is the Trail Backpack.
